title: Coil spring along a helix
purpose: Sweep a round wire along a helix with exact rotation-minimizing frames and flat end caps, giving a closed spring mesh. Use it for mechanical props, suspension parts and coiled cables.

entry_points.name: helix_frame
entry_points.summary: (tangent, normal, binormal) at helix angle t; the normal is the Frenet normal turned back by the accumulated torsion, which makes the frame rotation-minimizing (no twist about the tangent).

entry_points.name: coil_spring
entry_points.signature: coil_spring(coil_radius=0.5, pitch=0.25, turns=6.0, wire_radius=0.05, steps_per_turn=36, sides=10)
entry_points.summary: A closed spring mesh centred at the origin along Y.

entry_points.name: main
entry_points.summary: Command line: write the spring as .gltf or .obj and print a JSON summary.

parameters.name: coil_radius
parameters.meaning: Distance from the Y axis to the wire centre.

parameters.name: pitch
parameters.meaning: Rise per turn; keep it above twice the wire radius so turns do not touch.

parameters.name: steps_per_turn
parameters.meaning: Samples along the helix per turn.

outputs.content: one mesh with POSITION and NORMAL, indexed triangles
the same spring as Wavefront OBJ

limits: Turns touch or pass through each other when the pitch is below twice the wire radius; nothing checks this. The volume check allows 0.8 percent below cross-section times helix length, the loss from straight segments and tilted rings at 36 steps per turn. Ends are cut square to the wire (no ground flat ends). No texture coordinates. Cap vertices are separate from the wire ends, so the mesh is closed after welding.
technique_references: Helix Frenet frame with curvature R / (R^2 + b^2) and torsion b / (R^2 + b^2)
Rotation-minimizing frame by undoing the accumulated torsion
